blocks.text: Three shortcuts this week. **Pick the cheaper method** (node or mesh). **Swap sources** ($V$ + series $R$ ⇄ $I$ ∥ $R$). **Shrink a circuit to two numbers** a load can see: $V_{\mathrm{Th}}$ and $R_{\mathrm{Th}}$. In heights, every shortcut keeps the **terminal heights** and throws away the inside ones.

rows: a voltage source fixes a height; a current source fixes a mesh
same terminal height for every load; inside heights change
terminal $a$ sags $R_{\mathrm{Th}}$ volts per amp drawn

rows: **Node voltage = height** above the node you ground.
**Voltage source:** fixes a step. To ground, it fixes a height; between two unknown nodes, it is a rigid rod.
**Current source:** fixes a current, never a height.
**Unknown height → KCL there:** what flows in = what flows out. Resistor current $=\dfrac{\text{fall}}{R}$, always downhill.
**Power** = current × height change. Climbing delivers, falling absorbs.

blocks.title: Try it 1 · Node or mesh for a bridge? (Textbook P4.54)

items: A voltage source $v_s$ **in series** with $R$ ⇄ a current source $i_s=\dfrac{v_s}{R}$ **in parallel** with the same $R$. The arrow points to the $+$ end.
**Same terminal height for every load.** The inside is different: never take a source's power from the swapped circuit.
$R$ **across** an ideal voltage source: changes no other height (drop it; it still burns power). $R$ **in series** with an ideal current source: changes only the height between them (drop it).
Strategy: swap toward what you want; merge parallel current sources and series voltage sources; repeat; go back to the original for powers.

items: Seen from $a$–$b$, any linear circuit is **one step $V_{\mathrm{Th}}$ and one slope $R_{\mathrm{Th}}$**.
$V_{\mathrm{Th}}$ = height of $a$ with nothing attached. $I_N$ = current through a wire from $a$ to $b$.
$R_{\mathrm{Th}}=\dfrac{V_{\mathrm{Th}}}{I_N}$. Or: sources off (voltage → wire, current → gap), push $1\,\mathrm{A}$ into $a$, read $a$'s height.
A load draws $i$, so $a$ **sags**: $v_{ab}=V_{\mathrm{Th}}-R_{\mathrm{Th}}i$. Norton = the source transformation: $I_N$ ∥ $R_{\mathrm{Th}}$.
Ground $b$, so $a$'s height is $v_{ab}$ (if a node dips below $b$, ground the lowest node and subtract).
Dependent sources inside? Keep them on. That is Week 5 Topic 1.
